# v160.2.7 — Worker View-Only Access Audit

**Cycle**: `paneltec-v160.2.7`
**Date**: 2026-07-10
**Owner**: Auto-generated by the v160.2.7 migration audit.

## 1. Goal (from PRD)

> Grant workers view-only access org-wide. Audit all enabled Worker
> modules → backend endpoints → required permissions. Snapshot DB.
> Write idempotent script (`migrate_v160_2_7_worker_perms.py`) to
> grant view-only permissions (e.g., `swms.view`,
> `certifications.view`, `workers.view_own`) to the worker preset
> and backfill existing users.

## 4. Findings

1. **Every currently-enabled worker mobile module already has
   `view=True` in `ROLE_DEFAULTS["worker"]`.** The "grant view-only" step
   is a NO-OP at the code-level preset — no preset change required.
2. **No worker user carries a per-user override** that would deny
   `view` on any of those resources. No backfill deletions required.
3. **Team scoping unchanged.** Workers remain `team_view=False` on
   operational resources (they only see records where `created_by ==
   user.id`, per `TEAM_SCOPED_RESOURCES` in `permissions.py`). This
   preserves v159.2 privacy hardening.

## 5. What the migration actually does

Because the audit shows the invariant already holds, the migration
becomes a **defensive assertion + idempotent guardrail** rather than
a data-mutating backfill:

1. Snapshots `user_permissions` → `user_permissions_backup_v160_2_7`
   (idempotent — skips if already populated).
2. For every worker-role user, ensures **no `view: false` override
   exists** on any of the 9 view-gated resources in §3 above. If any
   are found (future drift), the offending override key is removed
   and the change logged.
3. Prints a JSON summary of enumerated users, snapshotted rows, and
   any denies cleared.

Re-running the script is a no-op once the invariant is satisfied.

## 6. Phase B (deferred — needs explicit approval)

The literal reading of "view-only access **org-wide**" could imply
granting `team_view=True` on operational read resources so a worker
sees *every* pre-start / hazard / incident submitted anywhere in the
org, not just their own. Doing that would **reverse the v159.2
team-scoping hardening** and expand data visibility for the worker
role by two orders of magnitude on active sites.

**Decision**: NOT applied automatically. Documenting here so the user
can green-light or veto in a follow-up cycle. If desired, the flip is
a one-line edit in `ROLE_DEFAULTS["worker"]` (add `"team_view": True`
on the 6 team-scoped read resources) plus a re-run of this migration.
